metadata.title: Belavadös Races Compendium — Current Canon
metadata.subtitle: Canon player race pages, racial bloodlines / lineages, mixed heritage, and complete in-book stat blocks with no legacy lookup requirements.

use_notes: Belavadös DOCX and ZIP files supply world lore, race families, creator-god doctrine, daily-life tone, and time conversion data.
Uploaded spell JSON and grimoire ZIP supply spell names, classes, casting fields, level tags, and school tags.
Uploaded D&D PDFs are used only for generalized play, adventure, encounter, monster-reference, and errata structure patterns; their named NPCs and locations are not imported.
The uploaded reference image is treated as a visual attachment with no additional rules text needed for these JSON outputs.

named_content_policy.rule: D&D book content is generalized only; named NPCs and named locations from uploaded D&D books are intentionally omitted.
applies_to: spell display names/descriptions when names contain setting-person eponyms
named_content_policy.does_not_remove: Belavadös setting terms, Belavadös deity names, ancestry names, system-neutral race/class terms, or player-facing rules terminology.

world_frame.title: Old Temple Ledger
world_frame.text: The public hymns remember creation as blessing. The older ledgers record appetite, design, bloodline, body, and use with colder handwriting.

creator_families.created_people_summary: Nebyrr is now recorded as the single creator-god of Humans, Near-Humans, and Mixed Heritage: Human, Half-Elf (choose an Elf Bloodline), Half-Orc (Human + Orc Lineage), Khoravar Half-Elf (choose an Elf Bloodline), Umbral Human. The public hymn calls this lineage and blessing; the older register reads like curated divine husbandry, sorting bodies, habitats, temperaments, and spirit-resonance so civilization, lineage, dynasties, marriage, inheritance, and social order never depends on one mortal pattern alone.

intro: How I use this family: I present these peoples through civilization, lineage, dynasties, marriage, inheritance, and social order. Every race in this family traces its creation to Nebyrr only in my Belavadös table guide.
categories.godDomain: Civilization, lineage, dynasties, marriage, inheritance, social order
categories.currentCanonDoctrine: Nebyrr is the sole creator-god assigned to Humans, Near-Humans, and Mixed Heritage: Human, Half-Elf (choose an Elven-Type), Half-Orc (Human + Orc ancestry), Khoravar Half-Elf (choose an Elven-Type), and Umbral Human. Human retains its five established lineage options. Half-Elf and Khoravar Half-Elf each choose one of 21 Elven-Type ancestries: the 15 Elf bloodlines or one of the six Kaluseban bloodlines.

traits.name: Resourceful
traits.text: Once per long rest, when you fail an ability check or saving throw, you can reroll the d20 and must use the new result.

traits.name: Skillful
traits.text: You gain proficiency in one skill of your choice. If your background already gives the same skill, choose a different skill.

traits.name: Versatile
traits.text: Choose one extra language, tool proficiency, or simple weapon proficiency at character creation.

traits.name: Adaptive Heritage
traits.text: At character creation, choose one skill, tool, language, sign language, or cultural contact tied to your homeland or family line. You are proficient in that choice or can use it fluently.

traits.name: Lineage Bridge
traits.text: You can read, mediate, and translate between the customs of your ancestry-linked cultures. Once per long rest, add 1d4 to a History, Insight, Persuasion, or Survival check involving those cultures.

traits.name: Signature Expression
traits.text: Choose one minor expression tied to the ancestry: a harmless sensory sign, a tool/language proficiency, one cantrip using your class spellcasting ability, or one 1/long rest movement burst. The choice is made at character creation and does not stack with another full ancestry package.

traits.name: Nebyrr's Mark
traits.text: Nebyrr’s imprint favors civilization, lineage, inheritance, social bonds, and negotiated order. Once per long rest, add 1d4 to a History, Insight, or Persuasion check involving family, law, status, or settlement custom.

races.name: Half-Elf
races.description: Half-elves are dual-natured beings born of human and elven lineage, often balancing ambition with longevity. They tend to struggle with identity but excel at diplomacy, adaptability, and bridging cultures.
classification_notes: Half-Elf stays in Human and Mixed Heritage. Each Half-Elf must record the exact Elf bloodline on the elven side.
selection_rules: choose the human/mixed heritage race first, then record the exact Elf bloodline for the elven side.
extra_notes: Required Elf Bloodline: Record the exact Elf bloodline chosen for the elven side of this ancestry before applying mixed-heritage rules.

races.description: Dragonborn are draconic humanoids born of ancient dragon lineage, elemental force, dynastic memory, and divine sovereignty. In Belavadös, a Dragonborn may carry traditional chromatic, metallic, or gem ancestry while also belonging to a Belavadös dragon-parentage lineage.
extra_notes: Combined Ability Rule: A Belavadös Dragonborn gains the traditional Dragonborn trait package and the parentage features of its Belavadös dragon lineage. The breath, resistance, perception, and flight expressions remain active as standard draconic inheritance; the parentage features add bloodline-specific magic, senses, movement, survival, social, and elemental gifts.

Belavadös Dragonborn Trait Framework: Ability Score Increase: Increase one ability score by 2 and another ability score by 1, or increase three different ability scores by 1 each.; Creature Type: You are a Humanoid with draconic ancestry.; Size: You are Medium.; Speed: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.; Darkvision: You can see in dim light within 60 feet as if it were bright light, and darkness as if it were dim light. You cannot discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.; Draconic Body: You have scaled skin, claws, a powerful tail, and facial ridges tied to your bloodline. Your claws are natural weapons that deal 1d6 slashing damage. You also have advantage on ability checks or saving throws made to keep your balance.; Winged Heritage: Your wings are part of your natural body. When you fall and are not incapacitated, you may use your reaction to reduce falling damage by an amount equal to five times your level. Starting at 5th level, you may fly for 1 minute at a flying speed equal to your walking speed. Once you use this flight, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.; Elemental Channeling: Choose one Dragonborn lineage. You gain its parentage ability package. When a lineage ability requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier, chosen when you select this race.; Ancestral Presence: You gain proficiency in one of the following skills: Arcana, History, Intimidation, Nature, Perception, or Religion.; Languages: You can speak, read, and write Common and Draconic.

races.name: Panolima
races.description: Living Embodiments of Elemental Harmony: Earth, Fire, Water, Air, and Aether.
classification_notes: Panolima is a parent race. Earth, Fire, Water, Air, and Aether are Panolima bloodlines/lineages, not separate top-level races.
extra_notes: Lore: The Panolimas are beings of elemental harmony . Their bodies are infused with one of the five primordial elemental threads: Earth, Fire, Water, Air, or Aether. Each individual exhibits physical traits reflecting their elemental affinity, from stone-like skin and mossy hair to flowing, water-like forms or luminous, energy-filled auras. They thrive in environments aligned with their element, drawing sustenance, vitality, and energy from landscapes, currents, storms, magma, or ley lines. Their movements, gestures, and even voices often carry the rhythm of their element, and they engage in ritual cleansing or meditation to maintain harmony with their elemental thread. Earth Panolimas have skin patterned like bark or stone, hair resembling moss or soil, and a deep-toned, rumbling voice. They require contact with solid terrain, forests, caves, or mountains to maintain vitality. Their abilities include sensing structural weaknesses, reinforcing the land, and enduring physical hardships with exceptional resilience. They can read terrain, detect mineral-rich soils, and manipulate stone or plant life to shape their surroundings. Fire Panolimas exhibit cracks like magma across their skin, ember-red hair, and glowing eyes. They rely on heat sources, volcanic activity, and exposure to flames to sustain energy. Their bodies radiate warmth and light, and they can manipulate molten materials, summon bursts of flame, and purify areas through fire.
Best Classes: Druid, Sorcerer, Cleric, Monk, Ranger, Wizard, Barbarian, or any class reflecting the chosen thread.

races.name: Gwynis
races.description: Dream-Born Ethereals of Illusion, Memory, and Psychic Insight.
extra_notes: Lore: Gwynises are ethereal, dream-born beings . Their appearances range widely, from tall, slender, shadow-touched figures to luminous, starlit forms with flowing, weightless hair and shifting, aurora-like or mist-like skin patterns that reflect thought, emotion, or ambient magical energy. Eyes vary from glowing moons and crystalline orbs to hollow voids or softly luminescent shades, capable of perceiving layers of reality, psychic echoes, or dreamscapes. Their bodies can phase between tangible and ghostly states, trailing wisps, shadowed tendrils, or dreamlike distortions that ripple with their movements, and their fingers and limbs are long, dexterous, and capable of absorbing mana, manipulating subtle forces, or projecting dream energy. Gwynises move with fluid grace and silent precision, able to influence perception, subtly manipulate emotion, or weave ephemeral illusions and constructs from thought, dream, and psychic resonance. They thrive in magical, artistic, or low-light environments, sustaining themselves through dream energy, meditation, ambient magic, or symbolic nourishment, while chaotic or harsh surroundings can diminish focus, well-being, and psychic attunement. Gwynises possess a versatile range of abilities that blend ethereal grace, dreamcraft, and subtle guardianship. They can obscure themselves, manipulate perception, cloud memory, or guide and protect others through psychic insight and dream influence. They are capable of lucid dreamcraft, weaving illusions, threading thought into reality, and sensing hidden truths or intentions in both waking and dream realms. Their physical and metaphysical forms are resilient, enduring environmental extremes while maintaining grace, or phasing through matter and shadows when needed. Some Gwynises manifest ephemeral or surreal adornments, levitating objects, flowing tattoos, or subtle elemental or celestial effects that mirror their inner state. They can influence emotion and perception through presence, pheromones, or vocal resonance, and their aura often bends reality subtly around them, inspiring awe, creativity, or reflection in observers.
Best Classes: Bard, Warlock, Sorcerer, Wizard, Cleric, Rogue, or any illusion/psychic support role.

races.name: Geisamahi
races.description: Small Ferretfolk Tinkerers, Scouts, and Clever Problem-Solvers.
classification_notes: Geisamahi belong with Animalfolk because they are ferretfolk and stoatlike people; their tinkering culture is flavor, not their race family.
extra_notes: Bloodlines / Lineages: Geisamahi (ferretfolk tinkerers, scouts, awakened mechanists, adaptive builders)

Lore: The Geisamahis are small, agile creatures . They resemble large ferrets or stoats but walk upright and possess opposable thumbs, allowing them to manipulate objects with precision. Their bodies are wiry and compact, built for speed, nimbleness, and the ability to navigate tight spaces, while their elongated snouts, expressive eyes, and twitching whiskers reflect their alertness and curiosity. Fur varies in earthy browns, fiery oranges, and snowy whites, often with individualized patterns, and many adorn themselves with small tools, belts, and pouches containing gadgets or relics. They are highly adaptable, thriving in forests, ruins, urban alleys, or other cluttered or complex environments, and they maintain mental sharpness through exploration, invention, and playful problem-solving. Geisamahis have heightened senses and dexterity, allowing them to detect hidden passages, traps, or valuable items that others might miss. They are quick learners and excel at crafting devices, tools, and improvised mechanisms to aid in survival or exploration. Their movements are fluid and acrobatic, capable of extended jumps, climbing, and rapid dashes, enabling them to evade danger or reach otherwise inaccessible areas. They possess a natural instinct for teamwork, often coordinating with kin or allies in subtle, synchronized ways. Their energy and vitality are maintained through frequent rest, light, energy-rich meals, and exposure to natural environments. Geisamahis exhibit keen awareness of their surroundings, sensing traps, subtle hazards, or changes in terrain that might threaten their safety. Their small stature and nimble frame allow them to slip unnoticed through gaps or under cover, and their reflexes enable rapid reactions to threats.
Best Classes: Rogue, Artificer, Ranger, Bard, Monk, Fighter, or any scout/tinker role.

races.name: Dril'thar
races.description: Amphibious Mystics of the Living Waters.
extra_notes: Lore: The Dril'thar are an ancient amphibious people whose civilizations rise from swamps, flooded jungles, coral reefs, mangrove coasts, subterranean rivers, mist-choked marshes, and sacred rainforests. Across countless regions of the world, they are known as healers, navigators, mystics, hunters, survivalists, and wandering pilgrims capable of thriving where most civilizations would collapse. To outsiders, Dril'thar are often misunderstood as poisonous frogfolk, territorial swamp-creatures, or eerie marsh spirits. In truth, they are one of the most biologically adaptable and spiritually complex peoples in existence. Their philosophy teaches that all things move in cycles: rain becomes river, river becomes sea, decay becomes renewal, and death feeds life anew. Water is not merely an element to the Dril'thar—it is memory, ancestry, spirit, and destiny itself. A spawning pool may serve simultaneously as temple, cemetery, and place of prophecy, for the Dril'thar believe the currents of the world carry the echoes of those who came before.
Best Classes: Ranger Monk

races.name: Tamhiogal
races.description: Aquatic Bettafolk of Hydromancy, Coral Stewardship, and Tidal Spirits.
extra_notes: Lore: Tamhiogal are aquatic beings. They resemble betta fish in their coloration, displaying vibrant shades of blues, purples, teals, and crimsons that shift with emotion and magical activity. On land, they possess scaled, graceful humanoid arms and legs, with scales rippling along their cheeks, necks, and collarbones. Their eyes are liquid and reflective, glowing faintly in dim light, and their hair consists of bioluminescent, jellyfish-like strands that can sting mildly when threatened. In water, they have gills along their necks, webbing between fingers and elbows, and fins along the spine, knees, and tail. Their legs are replaced by long, sleek caudal fins, with dorsal and anal fins enhancing maneuverability. Tamhiogal require hydration and tidal energy, which regenerate most efficiently in aquatic environments. They sustain themselves through fish, kelp, and other sea-based foods. Being immersed in water naturally maintains their hygiene and overall well-being. Exposure to polluted or stagnant water causes spiritual and emotional dissonance, while ritual bathing and communion with ocean spirits restore clarity, mood, and magical flow. Tamhiogal possess abilities attuned to both water and land. They can transition smoothly between terrestrial and aquatic forms, allowing fluid movement across both environments.
Best Classes: Druid, Cleric, Sorcerer, Bard, Ranger, Paladin, or any oceanic guardian role.

extra_notes: Lore: Tiny fungal raccoon-folk born from ancient symbiotic spores and scavenger spirits, Jaspey are eerie yet lovable creatures that blur the line between woodland fae, living fungus, and grave-born scavenger. Though their appearance often resembles tiny undead raccoons stitched together with moss, mushrooms, and decay, Jaspey are fully living beings with beating hearts, warm emotions, and vibrant cultures. Standing only a few inches tall, Jaspey can sleep inside coat pockets, teacups, backpacks, hollow books, hat brims, or even small tins. Entire hidden settlements may exist unnoticed inside old walls, cemetery gardens, forgotten cupboards, abandoned wagons, or the roots of ancient trees. Jaspey are natural scavengers, herbalists, healers, thieves, potion brewers, and strange little mystics. They collect shiny objects obsessively, form strong emotional bonds with larger companions, and often travel alongside adventuring parties as medics, alchemists, scouts, or magical nuisances.

races.name: Aburata
races.description: Infernal Dual-Form Equinefolk of Ambition, Hellfire, and Commanding Presence.
classification_notes: Aburata belongs in Miscellaneous and Hard-to-Classify because it crosses fiendish planar ancestry with equine-bodied traits.
extra_notes: Lore: The Aburatas are a race of infernal beings . They possess two distinct forms that reflect their dual nature: a humanoid form and a quadrupedal, equine-inspired form. In humanoid form, Aburatas have polished, taut skin resembling obsidian, molten iron, or amethyst-violet, often etched with glowing sigils or ember-like vein patterns that pulse with their emotions. Their eyes blaze with infernal fire or sink into abyssal voids, and their hair can range from jet black to flame-red, silver-violet, or stark white. Horns emerge in unique shapes such as spiraled, antlered, or blade-like, glowing faintly with infernal energy, while a prehensile tail flickers with embers or faint hellfire, aiding balance and expressive gestures. In quadrupedal form, their humanoid upper bodies transition into powerful horse-like torsos sheathed in scaled textures reminiscent of volcanic stone or blackened steel, with muscular limbs ending in broad hooves that leave glowing, smoldering prints. The tail grows longer and more expressive, capable of grasping objects or assisting in movements, while the air around them carries heat and shadow, enhancing their imposing presence. Their voices are resonant and hypnotic, capable of commanding attention or inspiring unease. Aburatas are sustained by infernal energy rather than ordinary nourishment, drawing vitality from places of power, fire-lit areas, or sites infused with dark influence. They maintain stamina, focus, and resilience through sheer will and magical energy, and their infernal heritage grants them natural resistance to fire, curses, and corruption. Aburatas are highly charismatic, their presence amplifying social influence, persuasion, and intimidation. They exhibit keen dexterity and precision in both combat and manipulation of objects, aided by sharp, clawed hands in humanoid form.
Best Classes: Warlock, Paladin, Bard, Sorcerer, Fighter, Rogue, or any charismatic commander role.

races.name: Volsarii
races.description: Four-Armed Ferriers of Souls, Liminal Balance, and Ethereal Wings.
classification_notes: Volsarii belongs in Miscellaneous and Hard-to-Classify because it crosses liminal, soul-ferrying, winged, and multi-limbed traits.
extra_notes: Lore: Volsariis are ethereal, multi-limbed beings . They possess four arms as a standard trait, elongated ears that curve upward and nearly resemble horns, and long, sensitive antennae atop their heads that detect changes in the environment, subtle emotions, and spiritual currents. Their skin ranges widely from iridescent shades of deep blues, greens, and storm-gray to luminous pastels, dawn-pinks, or shadowed violets, often streaked or veined with faint magical light, and may carry subtle markings that glow or shift with emotion, spiritual energy, or ambient magic. Their eyes vary from softly glowing gold, silver, and sky-blue to hollow voids, nebula-like patterns, or luminous starlight, reflecting both perception of the physical world and awareness of spirits, dream energy, or hidden currents. Hair flows lightly or appears almost weightless, with colors spanning metallic, pastel, starlit, or shadowed hues, sometimes giving the impression of liquid light, drifting mist, or feather-like strands. They maintain an elegant, deliberate grace in movement, capable of silent terrestrial motion, climbing, gliding, or, in their final life cycle, sprouting vast wings ranging from feathered to gossamer or ethereal forms, allowing them flight and aerial control that expresses both power and precision. Volsariis act as ferriers of the dead for Nyxarion, guiding souls through liminal spaces and maintaining the balance between life and death. They are attuned to both the waking and spiritual realms, able to sense, communicate with, and influence spirits, manage transitions, and preserve memory through subtle manipulation of energy, aura, or pheromones. Their abilities blend ethereal perception, dream- or shadow-influenced magic, and radiant or elemental powers, allowing them to phase through matter, weave illusions, manipulate light, wind, or celestial energies, and project calming, inspiring, or disorienting auras. Rituals, meditation, and communion with sacred or magical sites restore vitality, while harsh, chaotic, or energy-depleted environments can diminish focus and magical resonance. Volsariis draw sustenance primarily from ambient magic, spiritual energy, or dream currents rather than conventional food, though symbolic consumption may accompany ceremonial practices. Their culture emphasizes cycles, reflection, guardianship, guidance, and balance, blending artistic expression, dreamwork, and ritual observances with precise attention to the flow of life, death, and magical currents.
Best Classes: Cleric, Paladin, Warlock, Bard, Monk, Wizard, or any psychopomp/guardian role.

races.name: Deorbasun
races.description: Majestic Beast-Souled Guardians of Instinct, Honor, and Mystical Territory.
classification_notes: Deorbasun belongs in Miscellaneous and Hard-to-Classify because it crosses animal, guardian, mystical, and soul-animal traits.
extra_notes: Lore: Deorbasuns are majestic. Their physiques range from muscular, feline-like frames to lithe, agile forms with fur, scales, or earth-toned skin, reflecting a deep connection to predatory grace, wilderness instinct, and mystical energy. Heights vary widely, from six to nine feet, and their limbs are long and flexible, ending in retractable claws or talons capable of channeling energy or venom. Eyes glow with intelligence and authority, displaying hues from ember and gold to crystalline blues, greens, or silver, and often carry faint luminescence that responds to magic or emotion. Hair and manes vary from obsidian black, smoldering crimson, and radiant gold to bioluminescent strands, shimmered locks, or ethereal highlights, often adorned with beads, feathers, bones, or gemstones marking achievements, lineage, or ritual significance. Wings, tails, or subtle soul-animal traits enhance both presence and ability, with wings capable of flight or generating gusts, tails delivering venom, radiant energy, or prehensile utility, and faint ethereal markings or patterns tying form to instinct and magic. Deorbasuns possess extraordinary physical and magical abilities that blend predatory skill, shapeshifting versatility, and environmental attunement. They can leap with precision, maneuver through air or terrain with grace, and strike with claws, fangs, or tails imbued with energy or venom. Some can shift subtly to reflect traits of a soul-animal, such as enhanced senses, agility, or elemental affinities, while others maintain a consistently imposing, feline-like or beastly form. Their endurance and stamina are exceptional, allowing them to traverse rugged terrain, hunt, or perform ritualized movement for extended periods. They absorb energy through magical currents, prey, or ambient mana, and their focus and vitality are renewed through hunting, meditation, ritual exposure, or communion with natural and mystical environments. Deorbasuns are highly perceptive, capable of reading subtle environmental cues, sensing magical disturbances, and coordinating with wildlife or allies in ways that reflect both strategic intelligence and instinctual response.
Best Classes: Barbarian, Fighter, Ranger, Druid, Paladin, Monk, or any guardian/hunter role.

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.text: You can see in dim light within 60 ft. as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You cannot discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

traits.name: Fey Ancestry
traits.text: You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic cannot put you to sleep unless you willingly allow it.

traits.name: Fey Gift
traits.text: You carry a fey expression. You gain proficiency in Performance, Persuasion, Deception, or Nature, and can use one minor charm, glamour, luck, or misdirection effect once per long rest if the trait is magical.

traits.name: Lethargy Resilience
traits.text: You have advantage on saving throws against the ancestry’s signature hazard, condition, or environmental pressure. If a damage type is named, you also gain resistance to that damage type.

traits.name: Skill Versatility
traits.text: You gain proficiency in two skills of your choice. These proficiencies represent mixed cultural training and social adaptability.

traits.name: Adaptive Heritage
traits.text: At character creation, choose one skill, tool, language, sign language, or cultural contact tied to your homeland or family line. You are proficient in that choice or can use it fluently.

traits.name: Lineage Bridge
traits.text: You can read, mediate, and translate between the customs of your ancestry-linked cultures. Once per long rest, add 1d4 to a History, Insight, Persuasion, or Survival check involving those cultures.

traits.name: Signature Expression
traits.text: Choose one minor expression tied to the ancestry: a harmless sensory sign, a tool/language proficiency, one cantrip using your class spellcasting ability, or one 1/long rest movement burst. The choice is made at character creation and does not stack with another full ancestry package.

traits.name: Nebyrr's Mark
traits.text: Nebyrr’s imprint favors civilization, lineage, inheritance, social bonds, and negotiated order. Once per long rest, add 1d4 to a History, Insight, or Persuasion check involving family, law, status, or settlement custom.

traits.name: Elven ancestral thread
traits.text: This is the Elven ancestral thread ancestry feature. It grants one concrete benefit chosen from the stat block theme: proficiency in a matching skill/tool, a 1d4 bonus once per long rest to a matching check, a minor movement or sense adaptation, or a single limited magical expression if the feature is supernatural. It does not stack with another full ancestry block.

bloodlines.name: Half-Elf — Wood Elf

bloodlines.name: Half-Elf — Sea Elf
bloodlines.description: Half-Elf expression with the elven ancestral thread of Sea Elf. Half-elves are dual-natured beings born of human and elven lineage, often balancing ambition with longevity. They tend to struggle with identity but excel at diplomacy, adaptability, and bridging cultures. Aquatic elves adapted to life beneath the waves. They thrive in oceanic environments, maintaining deep cultural ties to marine ecosystems, reef civilizations, and seafaring alliances.

bloodlines.description: Half-Elf expression with the elven ancestral thread of Kaluseban. Half-elves are dual-natured beings born of human and elven lineage, often balancing ambition with longevity. They tend to struggle with identity but excel at diplomacy, adaptability, and bridging cultures. Elegant Mana-Bound Humanoids of Ley Lines, Nature, Moonlight, and Shadow.
classificationNotes: This is an Elf bloodline under the Elf parent race, not a separate race family.

Mana-Bound Vitality. You require periodic exposure to magical energy, sacred natural sites, ley lines, celestial light, ritual practice, or enchanted environments to remain fully balanced. statBlock.summary: player character bloodline / lineage block • Khoravar expression with the elven ancestral thread of Shadar-Kai. Khoravar are a refined mixed-heritage people often shaped by structured societies and cosmopolitan regions. They are known for blending martial discipline with intellectual or civic achievement. Shadow-bound elves tied to bleak or shadowy realms, often serving powerful entities of the Shadowfell. They are hardened, disciplined, and resilient due to their exposure to despair and entropy. This page contains the complete player-facing rules needed to select this option without opening any builder files.
statBlock.abilityScores: Belavadös Standard Ancestry Scores: increase one ability score by 2 and a different ability score by 1, or increase three different ability scores by 1. Recommended priorities: Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, Dexterity.
statBlock.languages: Common, Elvish, Sylvan.
statBlock.proficiencies: Skill proficiencies: Persuasion, History, Stealth, Perception. Additional proficiencies: ancestral weapon training named by the trait.
statBlock.senses: darkvision 60 ft.; passive Perception uses your Wisdom modifier and proficiency normally.

traits.name: Elf
traits.text: This is the Elf ancestry feature. It grants one concrete benefit chosen from the stat block theme: proficiency in a matching skill/tool, a 1d4 bonus once per long rest to a matching check, a minor movement or sense adaptation, or a single limited magical expression if the feature is supernatural. It does not stack with another full ancestry block.

traits.name: Blessing of the Raven Queen
traits.text: This is the Blessing of the Raven Queen ancestry feature. It grants one concrete benefit chosen from the stat block theme: proficiency in a matching skill/tool, a 1d4 bonus once per long rest to a matching check, a minor movement or sense adaptation, or a single limited magical expression if the feature is supernatural. It does not stack with another full ancestry block.

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.text: You can see in dim light within 60 ft. as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You cannot discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

traits.name: Fey Ancestry
traits.text: You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic cannot put you to sleep unless you willingly allow it.

traits.name: Keen Senses
traits.text: You gain proficiency in Perception. If you already have it, choose Insight, Investigation, Nature, or Survival instead.

traits.name: Necrotic Resistance
traits.text: You have resistance to necrotic damage.

traits.name: Trance
traits.text: You do not need ordinary sleep. Four hours of meditative rest can give you the benefit of a long rest when the rest of the party receives one normally.

traits.name: Fey Gift
traits.text: You carry a fey expression. You gain proficiency in Performance, Persuasion, Deception, or Nature, and can use one minor charm, glamour, luck, or misdirection effect once per long rest if the trait is magical.

traits.name: Lethargy Resilience
traits.text: You have advantage on saving throws against the ancestry’s signature hazard, condition, or environmental pressure. If a damage type is named, you also gain resistance to that damage type.

traits.name: Skill Versatility
traits.text: You gain proficiency in two skills of your choice. These proficiencies represent mixed cultural training and social adaptability.

traits.name: Adaptive Heritage
traits.text: At character creation, choose one skill, tool, language, sign language, or cultural contact tied to your homeland or family line. You are proficient in that choice or can use it fluently.

traits.name: Lineage Bridge
traits.text: You can read, mediate, and translate between the customs of your ancestry-linked cultures. Once per long rest, add 1d4 to a History, Insight, Persuasion, or Survival check involving those cultures.

traits.name: Signature Expression
traits.text: Choose one minor expression tied to the ancestry: a harmless sensory sign, a tool/language proficiency, one cantrip using your class spellcasting ability, or one 1/long rest movement burst. The choice is made at character creation and does not stack with another full ancestry package.

traits.name: Nebyrr's Mark
traits.text: Nebyrr’s imprint favors civilization, lineage, inheritance, social bonds, and negotiated order. Once per long rest, add 1d4 to a History, Insight, or Persuasion check involving family, law, status, or settlement custom.

traits.name: Fey Memory
traits.text: You carry a fey expression. You gain proficiency in Performance, Persuasion, Deception, or Nature, and can use one minor charm, glamour, luck, or misdirection effect once per long rest if the trait is magical.

traits.name: Graceful Hunter
traits.text: This is the Graceful Hunter ancestry feature. It grants one concrete benefit chosen from the stat block theme: proficiency in a matching skill/tool, a 1d4 bonus once per long rest to a matching check, a minor movement or sense adaptation, or a single limited magical expression if the feature is supernatural. It does not stack with another full ancestry block.

traits.name: Shadow Familiarity
traits.text: You gain proficiency in Stealth, or another skill if already proficient. In the terrain or lighting named by this trait, you can attempt to hide while lightly obscured and may add 1d4 to one Stealth check per short or long rest.

traits.name: Creator's Mark
traits.text: Your creator-god imprint shapes how the ancestry is read in Belavadös. Once per long rest, add 1d4 to an ability check tied to the creator-god domain shown on this page.

Darkvision: You can see in dim light within 60 ft. as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You cannot discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

Healing Hands: As an action once per long rest, touch a creature and restore hit points equal to your level or your proficiency bonus + your level, whichever your table prefers for this campaign tier.
Light Bearer: You know a light-producing cantrip. Charisma, Wisdom, or your class spellcasting ability is your spellcasting ability for it.

Celestial Revelation: Once per long rest, you can reveal a celestial form for 1 minute. Choose one expression tied to the lineage: radiant damage bonus, frightening presence, limited flight, or healing aura.
Fey Ancestry: You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic cannot put you to sleep unless you willingly allow it.

Fey Gift: You carry a fey expression. You gain proficiency in Performance, Persuasion, Deception, or Nature, and can use one minor charm, glamour, luck, or misdirection effect once per long rest if the trait is magical.

Lethargy Resilience: You have advantage on saving throws against the ancestry’s signature hazard, condition, or environmental pressure. If a damage type is named, you also gain resistance to that damage type.
Skill Versatility: You gain proficiency in two skills of your choice. These proficiencies represent mixed cultural training and social adaptability.

Adaptive Heritage: At character creation, choose one skill, tool, language, sign language, or cultural contact tied to your homeland or family line. You are proficient in that choice or can use it fluently.

Lineage Bridge: You can read, mediate, and translate between the customs of your ancestry-linked cultures. Once per long rest, add 1d4 to a History, Insight, Persuasion, or Survival check involving those cultures.

Signature Expression: Choose one minor expression tied to the ancestry: a harmless sensory sign, a tool/language proficiency, one cantrip using your class spellcasting ability, or one 1/long rest movement burst. The choice is made at character creation and does not stack with another full ancestry package.

Nebyrr's Mark: Nebyrr’s imprint favors civilization, lineage, inheritance, social bonds, and negotiated order. Once per long rest, add 1d4 to a History, Insight, or Persuasion check involving family, law, status, or settlement custom.

Fey Memory: You carry a fey expression. You gain proficiency in Performance, Persuasion, Deception, or Nature, and can use one minor charm, glamour, luck, or misdirection effect once per long rest if the trait is magical.

Graceful Hunter: This is the Graceful Hunter ancestry feature. It grants one concrete benefit chosen from the stat block theme: proficiency in a matching skill/tool, a 1d4 bonus once per long rest to a matching check, a minor movement or sense adaptation, or a single limited magical expression if the feature is supernatural. It does not stack with another full ancestry block.
Creator's Mark: Your creator-god imprint shapes how the ancestry is read in Belavadös. Once per long rest, add 1d4 to an ability check tied to the creator-god domain shown on this page.
Bloodline Expression: This trait supplies the named lineage’s body shape, cultural tell, and one appropriate mechanical expression from the traits listed in this stat block.

Sigrananna's Mark: This ancestry carries a visible or spiritual creator-god imprint. Once per long rest, add 1d4 to an ability check involving the Humans, Near-Humans, and Mixed Heritage themes, a native biome, or a culture that recognizes this mark.

bloodlines.name: Khoravar — Kaluseban
bloodlines.description: Khoravar expression with the elven ancestral thread of Kaluseban. Khoravar are a refined mixed-heritage people often shaped by structured societies and cosmopolitan regions. They are known for blending martial discipline with intellectual or civic achievement. Elegant Mana-Bound Humanoids of Ley Lines, Nature, Moonlight, and Shadow.
classificationNotes: This is an Elf bloodline under the Elf parent race, not a separate race family.

tableAbilities.summary: Ability Score Increase. Increase one ability score by 2 and another ability score by 1, or increase three different ability scores by 1 each.
Creature Type. You are a Humanoid.
Size. You are Medium.
Speed. Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

Mana-Bound Vitality. You require periodic exposure to magical energy, sacred natural sites, ley lines, celestial light, ritual practice, or enchanted environments to remain fully balanced. Long-term deprivation from magic may cause exhaustion, restlessness, or diminished spellcasting at the DM's discretion.

Bloodline Affinity. Choose one Kaluseban bloodline. You gain the bloodline gift listed for it.
Languages. You can speak, read, and write Common and one additional language tied to your home culture, bloodline, or magical tradition.

statBlock.summary: player character ancestry block • Elves are long-lived, graceful beings deeply attuned to magic, nature, and art. Their societies often value tradition, beauty, and refined mastery of specialized skills. They are broadly divided across many cultural and biological lineages throughout the worlds of the multiverse. This page contains the complete player-facing rules needed to select this option without opening any builder files.
statBlock.abilityScores: Belavadös Standard Ancestry Scores: increase one ability score by 2 and a different ability score by 1, or increase three different ability scores by 1. Recommended priorities: Dexterity, Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma.
statBlock.languages: Common and Elvish; add one local dialect when the settlement culture calls for it.
statBlock.proficiencies: Skill proficiencies: Persuasion, History, Survival, Arcana.
statBlock.senses: darkvision 60 ft.; passive Perception uses your Wisdom modifier and proficiency normally.

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.text: You can see in dim light within 60 ft. as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You cannot discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

traits.name: Elven Lineage
traits.text: This is the Elven Lineage ancestry feature. It grants one concrete benefit chosen from the stat block theme: proficiency in a matching skill/tool, a 1d4 bonus once per long rest to a matching check, a minor movement or sense adaptation, or a single limited magical expression if the feature is supernatural. It does not stack with another full ancestry block.

traits.name: Fey Ancestry
traits.text: You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic cannot put you to sleep unless you willingly allow it.

traits.name: Keen Senses
traits.text: You gain proficiency in Perception. If you already have it, choose Insight, Investigation, Nature, or Survival instead.

traits.name: Trance
traits.text: You do not need ordinary sleep. Four hours of meditative rest can give you the benefit of a long rest when the rest of the party receives one normally.

traits.name: Fey Memory
traits.text: You carry a fey expression. You gain proficiency in Performance, Persuasion, Deception, or Nature, and can use one minor charm, glamour, luck, or misdirection effect once per long rest if the trait is magical.

traits.name: Graceful Hunter
traits.text: This is the Graceful Hunter ancestry feature. It grants one concrete benefit chosen from the stat block theme: proficiency in a matching skill/tool, a 1d4 bonus once per long rest to a matching check, a minor movement or sense adaptation, or a single limited magical expression if the feature is supernatural. It does not stack with another full ancestry block.

traits.name: Bloodline Expression
traits.text: This trait supplies the named lineage’s body shape, cultural tell, and one appropriate mechanical expression from the traits listed in this stat block.

traits.name: Sigrananna's Mark
traits.text: This ancestry carries a visible or spiritual creator-god imprint. Once per long rest, add 1d4 to an ability check involving the Elf Parent Race and Elf Bloodlines themes, a native biome, or a culture that recognizes this mark.

traits.name: Trance

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.text: You can see in dim light within 60 ft. as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You cannot discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

traits.name: Elven Lineage
traits.text: This is the Elven Lineage ancestry feature. It grants one concrete benefit chosen from the stat block theme: proficiency in a matching skill/tool, a 1d4 bonus once per long rest to a matching check, a minor movement or sense adaptation, or a single limited magical expression if the feature is supernatural. It does not stack with another full ancestry block.

traits.name: Fey Ancestry
traits.text: You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic cannot put you to sleep unless you willingly allow it.

traits.name: Keen Senses
traits.text: You gain proficiency in Perception. If you already have it, choose Insight, Investigation, Nature, or Survival instead.

traits.name: Trance
traits.text: You do not need ordinary sleep. Four hours of meditative rest can give you the benefit of a long rest when the rest of the party receives one normally.

traits.name: Fey Memory
traits.text: You carry a fey expression. You gain proficiency in Performance, Persuasion, Deception, or Nature, and can use one minor charm, glamour, luck, or misdirection effect once per long rest if the trait is magical.

traits.name: Graceful Hunter
traits.text: This is the Graceful Hunter ancestry feature. It grants one concrete benefit chosen from the stat block theme: proficiency in a matching skill/tool, a 1d4 bonus once per long rest to a matching check, a minor movement or sense adaptation, or a single limited magical expression if the feature is supernatural. It does not stack with another full ancestry block.

traits.name: Shadow Familiarity
traits.text: You gain proficiency in Stealth, or another skill if already proficient. In the terrain or lighting named by this trait, you can attempt to hide while lightly obscured and may add 1d4 to one Stealth check per short or long rest.

traits.name: Creator's Mark
traits.text: Your creator-god imprint shapes how the ancestry is read in Belavadös. Once per long rest, add 1d4 to an ability check tied to the creator-god domain shown on this page.

traits.name: Bloodline Expression
traits.text: This trait supplies the named lineage’s body shape, cultural tell, and one appropriate mechanical expression from the traits listed in this stat block.

traits.name: Sigrananna's Mark
traits.text: This ancestry carries a visible or spiritual creator-god imprint. Once per long rest, add 1d4 to an ability check involving the Elf Parent Race and Elf Bloodlines themes, a native biome, or a culture that recognizes this mark.

bloodlines.name: Kaluseban
bloodlines.description: Elegant Mana-Bound Humanoids of Ley Lines, Nature, Moonlight, and Shadow.
classificationNotes: This is an Elf bloodline under the Elf parent race, not a separate race family.

tableAbilities.summary: Ability Score Increase. Increase one ability score by 2 and another ability score by 1, or increase three different ability scores by 1 each.
Creature Type. You are a Humanoid.
Size. You are Medium.
Speed. Your base walking speed is 30 feet.

Mana-Bound Vitality. You require periodic exposure to magical energy, sacred natural sites, ley lines, celestial light, ritual practice, or enchanted environments to remain fully balanced. Long-term deprivation from magic may cause exhaustion, restlessness, or diminished spellcasting at the DM's discretion.

Leyline Sense. You gain proficiency in Arcana or Nature. You can sense whether a place has strong natural, celestial, arcane, shadow, aquatic, or earthen magical resonance after spending 1 minute in quiet focus.

Subtle Channeling. You know one cantrip of your choice from the druid, cleric, or wizard spell list. Wisdom, Intelligence, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for it, chosen when you select this race.
Ritual Poise. You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed by illusions, dream effects, or magic that distorts your perception of reality.
Bloodline Affinity. Choose one Kaluseban bloodline. You gain the bloodline gift listed for it.
Languages. You can speak, read, and write Common and one additional language tied to your home culture, bloodline, or magical tradition.

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.text: You can see in dim light within 60 ft. as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You cannot discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

traits.name: Fey Ancestry
traits.text: You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic cannot put you to sleep unless you willingly allow it.

traits.name: Long-Limbed
traits.text: This is the Long-Limbed ancestry feature. It grants one concrete benefit chosen from the stat block theme: proficiency in a matching skill/tool, a 1d4 bonus once per long rest to a matching check, a minor movement or sense adaptation, or a single limited magical expression if the feature is supernatural. It does not stack with another full ancestry block.

traits.name: Powerful Build
traits.text: You count as one size larger when determining carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.

traits.name: Sneaky
traits.text: This is the Sneaky ancestry feature. It grants one concrete benefit chosen from the stat block theme: proficiency in a matching skill/tool, a 1d4 bonus once per long rest to a matching check, a minor movement or sense adaptation, or a single limited magical expression if the feature is supernatural. It does not stack with another full ancestry block.

traits.name: Surprise Attack

It grants one concrete benefit chosen from the stat block theme: proficiency in a matching skill/tool, a 1d4 bonus once per long rest to a matching check, a minor movement or sense adaptation, or a single limited magical expression if the feature is supernatural. It does not stack with another full ancestry block.

traits.name: Survival Grit
traits.text: This is the Survival Grit ancestry feature. It grants one concrete benefit chosen from the stat block theme: proficiency in a matching skill/tool, a 1d4 bonus once per long rest to a matching check, a minor movement or sense adaptation, or a single limited magical expression if the feature is supernatural. It does not stack with another full ancestry block.

traits.name: Warband Instinct
traits.text: You gain proficiency in Perception or Survival. When the check uses the sense or instinct named by this trait, add 1d4 once per short or long rest.

traits.name: Hard-Won Presence
traits.text: You gain proficiency in Intimidation, Performance, or Persuasion. Once per long rest, add 1d4 to a social check where the ancestry’s presence, voice, or omen matters.

traits.name: Enkirael's Mark
traits.text: This ancestry carries a visible or spiritual creator-god imprint. Once per long rest, add 1d4 to an ability check involving the Orcs, Goblins, and Goblinoid Kin themes, a native biome, or a culture that recognizes this mark.

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.text: You can see in dim light within 60 ft. as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You cannot discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

traits.name: Fey Ancestry
traits.text: You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic cannot put you to sleep unless you willingly allow it.

traits.name: Fury of the Small
traits.text: When you damage a creature larger than you, you can deal extra damage equal to your proficiency bonus. You can use this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

traits.name: Nimble Escape
traits.text: You can take the Disengage or Hide action as a bonus action on your turn a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

traits.name: Survival Grit
traits.text: This is the Survival Grit ancestry feature. It grants one concrete benefit chosen from the stat block theme: proficiency in a matching skill/tool, a 1d4 bonus once per long rest to a matching check, a minor movement or sense adaptation, or a single limited magical expression if the feature is supernatural. It does not stack with another full ancestry block.

traits.name: Warband Instinct
traits.text: You gain proficiency in Perception or Survival. When the check uses the sense or instinct named by this trait, add 1d4 once per short or long rest.

traits.name: Hard-Won Presence
traits.text: You gain proficiency in Intimidation, Performance, or Persuasion. Once per long rest, add 1d4 to a social check where the ancestry’s presence, voice, or omen matters.

traits.name: Enkirael's Mark
traits.text: This ancestry carries a visible or spiritual creator-god imprint. Once per long rest, add 1d4 to an ability check involving the Orcs, Goblins, and Goblinoid Kin themes, a native biome, or a culture that recognizes this mark.

Primary Traits: Firbolg Magic: You know one cantrip or minor supernatural effect tied to this ancestry. If a leveled effect is listed, you can use it once per long rest. Use your class spellcasting ability, or Charisma if you have none.

Hidden Step: This is the Hidden Step ancestry feature. It grants one concrete benefit chosen from the stat block theme: proficiency in a matching skill/tool, a 1d4 bonus once per long rest to a matching check, a minor movement or sense adaptation, or a single limited magical expression if the feature is supernatural. It does not stack with another full ancestry block.
Powerful Build: You count as one size larger when determining carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.

Speech of Beast and Leaf: This is the Speech of Beast and Leaf ancestry feature. It grants one concrete benefit chosen from the stat block theme: proficiency in a matching skill/tool, a 1d4 bonus once per long rest to a matching check, a minor movement or sense adaptation, or a single limited magical expression if the feature is supernatural. It does not stack with another full ancestry block.

Burden Strength: This is the Burden Strength ancestry feature. It grants one concrete benefit chosen from the stat block theme: proficiency in a matching skill/tool, a 1d4 bonus once per long rest to a matching check, a minor movement or sense adaptation, or a single limited magical expression if the feature is supernatural. It does not stack with another full ancestry block.
Colossal Bearing: You gain proficiency in Perception or Survival. When the check uses the sense or instinct named by this trait, add 1d4 once per short or long rest.

Mountain Memory: You gain proficiency in Arcana, History, Nature, or Religion. Once per long rest, when you fail an Intelligence check using that proficiency, you can add 1d4 and potentially turn the failure into a success.

Anubaldir's Mark: This ancestry carries a visible or spiritual creator-god imprint. Once per long rest, add 1d4 to an ability check involving the Giantkin and Powerful Humanoids themes, a native biome, or a culture that recognizes this mark.

races.name: Dragonborn
races.description: Dragonborn are draconic humanoids born of ancient dragon lineage, elemental force, dynastic memory, and divine sovereignty. In Belavadös, a Dragonborn may carry traditional chromatic, metallic, or gem ancestry while also belonging to a Belavadös dragon-parentage lineage.
extraNotes: Combined Ability Rule: A Belavadös Dragonborn gains the traditional Dragonborn trait package and the parentage features of its Belavadös dragon lineage. The breath, resistance, perception, and flight expressions remain active as standard draconic inheritance; the parentage features add bloodline-specific magic, senses, movement, survival, social, and elemental gifts.

Belavadös Dragonborn Trait Framework: Ability Score Increase: Increase one ability score by 2 and another ability score by 1, or increase three different ability scores by 1 each.; Creature Type: You are a Humanoid with draconic ancestry.; Size: You are Medium.; Speed: Your base walking speed is 30 feet.; Darkvision: You can see in dim light within 60 feet as if it were bright light, and darkness as if it were dim light. You cannot discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.; Draconic Body: You have scaled skin, claws, a powerful tail, and facial ridges tied to your bloodline. Your claws are natural weapons that deal 1d6 slashing damage. You also have advantage on ability checks or saving throws made to keep your balance.; Winged Heritage: Your wings are part of your natural body. When you fall and are not incapacitated, you may use your reaction to reduce falling damage by an amount equal to five times your level. Starting at 5th level, you may fly for 1 minute at a flying speed equal to your walking speed. Once you use this flight, you cannot do so again until you finish a long rest.; Elemental Channeling: Choose one Dragonborn lineage. You gain its parentage ability package. When a lineage ability requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier, chosen when you select this race.; Ancestral Presence: You gain proficiency in one of the following skills: Arcana, History, Intimidation, Nature, Perception, or Religion.; Languages: You can speak, read, and write Common and Draconic.

Belavadös Dragon-Parentage Lineages: Noitzideq (Air and Weather): parent dragons Asaafi + Sauqonsex, with Boisein storm influence; inherited theme Sky, weather, air/wind, storm movement, and healing currents.; profile Neutral Coordinator; scores Altruism 2000, Lawfulness 1650, Cooperation 2200, Honor 1850; Saelftum (Volcanic Flame): parent dragons Erymasos + Oreilhya, with Zrom elemental pressure; inherited theme Fire, heat, molten resilience, temperature control, and volcanic endurance.; profile Lawful Defender; scores Altruism 1650, Lawfulness 2050, Cooperation 1700, Honor 1750; Jazwed (Lava and Crystal): parent dragons Erymasos + Nenshexeq + Zrom; inherited theme Fire, stone, crystal force, elemental shaping, and defensive engineering.; profile Lawful Enforcer; scores Altruism 1600, Lawfulness 2100, Cooperation 1550, Honor 1700; Khoalaros (Tide and Ocean): parent dragons Philous + Xuqhuath + Yichah; inherited theme Sea control, water shaping, currents, swimming grace, aquatic communication, and healing water.; profile Neutral Guardian; scores Altruism 2050, Lawfulness 1500, Cooperation 2100, Honor 2000; Gauksneth (Desert Sand and Hidden Water): parent dragons Innoxia + Nenshexeq + Yichah/Xuqhuath; inherited theme Earth shaping, stone sense, sand survival, hidden-water detection, and oasis stewardship.; profile Lawful Coordinator; scores Altruism 1700, Lawfulness 2200, Cooperation 2050, Honor 1600; Tuorszom (Stone and Mountain): parent dragons Nenshexeq + Innoxia + Aloic; inherited theme Stone control, earth shaping, metal/mineral awareness, tremor sense, and mountain endurance.; profile Lawful Sentinel; scores Altruism 1800, Lawfulness 2300, Cooperation 1600, Honor 2250; Taudinax (Shadow and Light): parent dragons Ekhoq + Pteris + Xacuacsih/Thusekha, with Kiczi illusion influence; inherited theme Shadow manipulation, darkness, illusion, tactical concealment, and controlled light.; profile Neutral Strategist; scores Altruism 1450, Lawfulness 1300, Cooperation 1450, Honor 1350; Gouxelq (Metal and Crystal): parent dragons Aloic + Nenshexeq + Zrom; inherited theme Metal control, stone/crystal shaping, elemental structure, and crafted barriers.; profile Lawful Coordinator; scores Altruism 1750, Lawfulness 2300, Cooperation 2250, Honor 1700; Vautaces (Radiance and Foresight): parent dragons Thusekha + Xacuacsih + Mumh + Lunngha/Eecors + Chiellieds; inherited theme Light control, radiant protection, perception, foresight, time-sense, and emotional insight.; profile Lawful Arbiter; scores Altruism 1900, Lawfulness 2150, Cooperation 1550, Honor 2300.

statBlock.abilityScores: Belavadös Standard Ancestry Scores: increase one ability score by 2 and a different ability score by 1, or increase three different ability scores by 1. Recommended priorities: Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Wisdom.
statBlock.languages: Common and Draconic or the relevant reptilian/amphibious local speech.
statBlock.proficiencies: Skill proficiencies: Stealth, Perception, Religion, Survival.
statBlock.senses: darkvision 60 ft.; passive Perception uses your Wisdom modifier and proficiency normally.

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.text: You can see in dim light within 60 ft. as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You cannot discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

traits.name: Draconic Cry
traits.text: As a bonus action, choose enemies within 10 ft. of you. Until the start of your next turn, your allies have advantage on the first attack roll they make against one affected enemy. Uses equal your proficiency bonus per long rest.

traits.name: Kobold Legacy
traits.text: This is the Kobold Legacy ancestry feature. It grants one concrete benefit chosen from the stat block theme: proficiency in a matching skill/tool, a 1d4 bonus once per long rest to a matching check, a minor movement or sense adaptation, or a single limited magical expression if the feature is supernatural. It does not stack with another full ancestry block.

traits.name: Ancient Blood
traits.text: This is the Ancient Blood ancestry feature. It grants one concrete benefit chosen from the stat block theme: proficiency in a matching skill/tool, a 1d4 bonus once per long rest to a matching check, a minor movement or sense adaptation, or a single limited magical expression if the feature is supernatural. It does not stack with another full ancestry block.

traits.name: Sovereign Presence
traits.text: You gain proficiency in Intimidation, Performance, or Persuasion. Once per long rest, add 1d4 to a social check where the ancestry’s presence, voice, or omen matters.

traits.name: Scaled Instinct
traits.text: You gain proficiency in Perception or Survival. When the check uses the sense or instinct named by this trait, add 1d4 once per short or long rest.

traits.name: Valkhamesh's Mark
traits.text: This ancestry carries a visible or spiritual creator-god imprint. Once per long rest, add 1d4 to an ability check involving the Draconic and Reptilian Races themes, a native biome, or a culture that recognizes this mark.

statBlock.lineageOrBloodlineUse: Use this block directly for this selection. If the parent race has a separate bloodline / lineage menu, choose exactly one bloodline / lineage block and do not stack multiple bloodlines unless a mixed-heritage record explicitly says to do so.

races.name: Fey-Folk
races.description: Fey-Folk are peoples shaped by glamour, luck, tiny or otherworldly bodies, dreamlike emotion, and trickster magic. At my table, Faerie, Fairy, and Gandirosha are not separate top-level races here; they are bloodlines of one Fey-Folk parent race. Players choose the Fey-Folk parent race, then choose the bloodline that defines body shape, magic, movement, culture, and table-facing traits.
classificationNotes: Faerie, Fairy, and Gandirosha are bloodlines of this parent race in this JSON structure.
This parent race keeps the shared fey baseline; the selected bloodline supplies the specific expression.

races.dmHook: Use Fey-Folk NPCs to show how Thalunesh's single-creator doctrine appears through fey bargains, celebrations, social masks, dream logic, luck, temptation, and playful danger.

statBlock.summary: player character ancestry block • Fey-Folk are peoples shaped by glamour, luck, tiny or otherworldly bodies, dreamlike emotion, and trickster magic. At my table, Faerie, Fairy, and Gandirosha are not separate top-level races here; they are bloodlines of one Fey-Folk parent race. Players choose the Fey-Folk parent race, then choose the bloodline that defines body shape, magic, movement, culture, and table-facing traits. This page contains the complete player-facing rules needed to select this option without opening any builder files.

bloodlines.name: Gandirosha
bloodlines.description: Luck-Touched Wanderers of Charm, Timing, and Subtle Magic.
classificationNotes: Gandirosha is treated as a Fey-Folk bloodline in this standard Belavadös category JSON, not as a separate top-level race.
Use the Fey-Folk parent race baseline plus this bloodline's stat block, traits, alignment tendency, and biome profile.
extraNotes: Lore: Gandiroshas are a race of magical, agile beings . Their presence in Belavadös is defined by charm, intuition, and a deep attunement to both chance and the subtle flows of magic in their environment. They range from petite to tall, standing between three and six feet, with wiry or lithe builds suited to quick movement, climbing, and graceful gestures. Their skin carries a natural, faint glow that can take the form of star-like freckles, soft sigils, or flowing patterns that shift with emotion, magical activity, or sunlight. Hair ranges from honey and chestnut to copper, gold, and jade tones, often styled in flowing waves, curls, or dramatic braids, adorned with charms, beads, or small enchanted trinkets that reflect personal flair and magical presence. Eyes are expressive and varied, including amber, hazel, deep brown, gold, green, or soft blue, capable of subtle luminescence when Gandiroshas focus their magical or intuitive senses. Their clothing blends practicality with artistry, often layered, flowing, or accented with pouches, charms, and symbols, allowing both freedom of movement and the display of individual style. Gandiroshas possess an innate connection to luck, opportunity, and the hidden currents of events around them, allowing them to sense favorable outcomes, detect subtle threats, and influence social or magical situations through intuition, charm, and clever timing. They move with remarkable lightness and agility, slipping past obstacles, navigating crowded spaces, or disappearing briefly from sight with fleeting illusions or environmental blending. Their social skills are heightened, drawing vitality and focus from interaction, shared meals, stories, music, or companionship, while isolation, stress, or chaotic surroundings can diminish their magical acuity. Gandiroshas have finely tuned perception, enabling them to read intentions, uncover hidden treasures, detect traps, and anticipate outcomes with uncanny accuracy. Their subtle magic can influence luck, create brief illusions, manipulate small objects, or enhance group morale through presence and charisma.
Best Classes: Bard, Rogue, Ranger, Monk, Warlock, Sorcerer, or any face/scout role.

races.playerGuidance: This parent-race baseline is intentionally flexible. The chosen bloodline/lineage gives the stronger inherited expression.
races.dmHook: Use Elemental Kin NPCs to show how Horundar creates different elemental expressions inside one people rather than treating every element as a separate ancestry family.

bloodlines.name: Flamekin
bloodlines.description: Small, volatile beings of concentrated fire essence, Flamekin flicker with unstable inner heat that reflects their emotions. They are quick to act and quick to burn out if not tempered.

races.name: Panolima
races.description: Living Embodiments of Elemental Harmony: Earth, Fire, Water, Air, and Aether.
classificationNotes: Panolima is a parent race. Earth, Fire, Water, Air, and Aether are Panolima bloodlines/lineages, not separate top-level races.
extraNotes: Lore: The Panolimas are beings of elemental harmony . Their bodies are infused with one of the five primordial elemental threads: Earth, Fire, Water, Air, or Aether. Each individual exhibits physical traits reflecting their elemental affinity, from stone-like skin and mossy hair to flowing, water-like forms or luminous, energy-filled auras. They thrive in environments aligned with their element, drawing sustenance, vitality, and energy from landscapes, currents, storms, magma, or ley lines. Their movements, gestures, and even voices often carry the rhythm of their element, and they engage in ritual cleansing or meditation to maintain harmony with their elemental thread. Earth Panolimas have skin patterned like bark or stone, hair resembling moss or soil, and a deep-toned, rumbling voice. They require contact with solid terrain, forests, caves, or mountains to maintain vitality. Their abilities include sensing structural weaknesses, reinforcing the land, and enduring physical hardships with exceptional resilience. They can read terrain, detect mineral-rich soils, and manipulate stone or plant life to shape their surroundings. Fire Panolimas exhibit cracks like magma across their skin, ember-red hair, and glowing eyes. They rely on heat sources, volcanic activity, and exposure to flames to sustain energy. Their bodies radiate warmth and light, and they can manipulate molten materials, summon bursts of flame, and purify areas through fire.
Best Classes: Druid, Sorcerer, Cleric, Monk, Ranger, Wizard, Barbarian, or any class reflecting the chosen thread.
races.dmHook: Use Panolima NPCs to show how Horundar's single-creator doctrine appears through Elemental and Energy-Born Peoples: ancestry, culture, reputation, temptation, and divine backlash.

races.name: Gwynis
races.description: Dream-Born Ethereals of Illusion, Memory, and Psychic Insight.
extraNotes: Lore: Gwynises are ethereal, dream-born beings . Their appearances range widely, from tall, slender, shadow-touched figures to luminous, starlit forms with flowing, weightless hair and shifting, aurora-like or mist-like skin patterns that reflect thought, emotion, or ambient magical energy. Eyes vary from glowing moons and crystalline orbs to hollow voids or softly luminescent shades, capable of perceiving layers of reality, psychic echoes, or dreamscapes. Their bodies can phase between tangible and ghostly states, trailing wisps, shadowed tendrils, or dreamlike distortions that ripple with their movements, and their fingers and limbs are long, dexterous, and capable of absorbing mana, manipulating subtle forces, or projecting dream energy. Gwynises move with fluid grace and silent precision, able to influence perception, subtly manipulate emotion, or weave ephemeral illusions and constructs from thought, dream, and psychic resonance. They thrive in magical, artistic, or low-light environments, sustaining themselves through dream energy, meditation, ambient magic, or symbolic nourishment, while chaotic or harsh surroundings can diminish focus, well-being, and psychic attunement. Gwynises possess a versatile range of abilities that blend ethereal grace, dreamcraft, and subtle guardianship. They can obscure themselves, manipulate perception, cloud memory, or guide and protect others through psychic insight and dream influence. They are capable of lucid dreamcraft, weaving illusions, threading thought into reality, and sensing hidden truths or intentions in both waking and dream realms. Their physical and metaphysical forms are resilient, enduring environmental extremes while maintaining grace, or phasing through matter and shadows when needed. Some Gwynises manifest ephemeral or surreal adornments, levitating objects, flowing tattoos, or subtle elemental or celestial effects that mirror their inner state. They can influence emotion and perception through presence, pheromones, or vocal resonance, and their aura often bends reality subtly around them, inspiring awe, creativity, or reflection in observers.
Best Classes: Bard, Warlock, Sorcerer, Wizard, Cleric, Rogue, or any illusion/psychic support role.
races.dmHook: Use Gwynis NPCs to show how Raeshkul's single-creator doctrine appears through Psionic, Astral, and Alien Minds: ancestry, culture, reputation, temptation, and divine backlash.

traits.name: Cat's Claws
traits.text: You have a climb speed and natural claws. The claws deal 1d6 + Strength or Dexterity modifier slashing damage.

traits.name: Cat's Talents
traits.text: You gain proficiency in Perception and Stealth, or one of those plus Acrobatics if you already have either proficiency.

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.text: You can see in dim light within 60 ft. as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You cannot discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

traits.name: Feline Agility
traits.text: When you move on your turn, you can double your speed until the end of the turn. You cannot use this again until you move 0 feet on one of your turns.

traits.name: Animal Gift
traits.text: This is the Animal Gift ancestry feature. It grants one concrete benefit chosen from the stat block theme: proficiency in a matching skill/tool, a 1d4 bonus once per long rest to a matching check, a minor movement or sense adaptation, or a single limited magical expression if the feature is supernatural. It does not stack with another full ancestry block.

traits.name: Beast Kinship
traits.text: This is the Beast Kinship ancestry feature. It grants one concrete benefit chosen from the stat block theme: proficiency in a matching skill/tool, a 1d4 bonus once per long rest to a matching check, a minor movement or sense adaptation, or a single limited magical expression if the feature is supernatural. It does not stack with another full ancestry block.

traits.name: Instinctive Survival
traits.text: You gain proficiency in Perception or Survival. When the check uses the sense or instinct named by this trait, add 1d4 once per short or long rest.

traits.name: Iskareth's Mark
traits.text: This ancestry carries a visible or spiritual creator-god imprint. Once per long rest, add 1d4 to an ability check involving the Animalfolk and Mammalian Anthropomorphs themes, a native biome, or a culture that recognizes this mark.

Primary Traits: +2 Dexterity: Ability score adjustment: +2 Dexterity. This adjustment is already included in the ability score line of this stat block.
-2 Strength: Ability score adjustment: -2 Strength. This adjustment is already included in the ability score line of this stat block.
Darkvision: You can see in dim light within 60 ft. as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You cannot discern color in darkness, only shades of gray.

Grounded Celestial: You carry a light-aspected expression. You can create harmless light, gain a fitting resistance or revelation if listed, and may add 1d4 to one Insight, Medicine, or Persuasion check per long rest.

Sharp Tusks: You have the natural weapon named by this trait. It deals 1d4 or 1d6 damage of the fitting type plus Strength or Dexterity modifier. If the trait also names poison, venom, grappling, or pushing, that rider can be used once per turn or proficiency-bonus times per long rest.
Telepathic: You can communicate telepathically with a creature you can see within 30 ft. This does not allow the creature to reply unless it also has telepathy.

Animal Gift: This is the Animal Gift ancestry feature. It grants one concrete benefit chosen from the stat block theme: proficiency in a matching skill/tool, a 1d4 bonus once per long rest to a matching check, a minor movement or sense adaptation, or a single limited magical expression if the feature is supernatural. It does not stack with another full ancestry block.

Beast Kinship: This is the Beast Kinship ancestry feature. It grants one concrete benefit chosen from the stat block theme: proficiency in a matching skill/tool, a 1d4 bonus once per long rest to a matching check, a minor movement or sense adaptation, or a single limited magical expression if the feature is supernatural. It does not stack with another full ancestry block.
Instinctive Survival: You gain proficiency in Perception or Survival. When the check uses the sense or instinct named by this trait, add 1d4 once per short or long rest.

Iskareth's Mark: This ancestry carries a visible or spiritual creator-god imprint. Once per long rest, add 1d4 to an ability check involving the Animalfolk and Mammalian Anthropomorphs themes, a native biome, or a culture that recognizes this mark.

races.name: Geisamahi
races.description: Small Ferretfolk Tinkerers, Scouts, and Clever Problem-Solvers.
classificationNotes: Geisamahi belong with Animalfolk because they are ferretfolk and stoatlike people; their tinkering culture is flavor, not their race family.
extraNotes: Bloodlines / Lineages: Geisamahi (ferretfolk tinkerers, scouts, awakened mechanists, adaptive builders)

Lore: The Geisamahis are small, agile creatures . They resemble large ferrets or stoats but walk upright and possess opposable thumbs, allowing them to manipulate objects with precision. Their bodies are wiry and compact, built for speed, nimbleness, and the ability to navigate tight spaces, while their elongated snouts, expressive eyes, and twitching whiskers reflect their alertness and curiosity. Fur varies in earthy browns, fiery oranges, and snowy whites, often with individualized patterns, and many adorn themselves with small tools, belts, and pouches containing gadgets or relics. They are highly adaptable, thriving in forests, ruins, urban alleys, or other cluttered or complex environments, and they maintain mental sharpness through exploration, invention, and playful problem-solving. Geisamahis have heightened senses and dexterity, allowing them to detect hidden passages, traps, or valuable items that others might miss. They are quick learners and excel at crafting devices, tools, and improvised mechanisms to aid in survival or exploration. Their movements are fluid and acrobatic, capable of extended jumps, climbing, and rapid dashes, enabling them to evade danger or reach otherwise inaccessible areas. They possess a natural instinct for teamwork, often coordinating with kin or allies in subtle, synchronized ways. Their energy and vitality are maintained through frequent rest, light, energy-rich meals, and exposure to natural environments. Geisamahis exhibit keen awareness of their surroundings, sensing traps, subtle hazards, or changes in terrain that might threaten their safety. Their small stature and nimble frame allow them to slip unnoticed through gaps or under cover, and their reflexes enable rapid reactions to threats.
Best Classes: Rogue, Artificer, Ranger, Bard, Monk, Fighter, or any scout/tinker role.
races.dmHook: Use Geisamahi NPCs to show how Iskareth's single-creator doctrine appears through Animalfolk and Mammalian Anthropomorphs: ancestry, culture, reputation, temptation, and divine backlash.

statBlock.summary: player character ancestry block • Small amphibious frogfolk with toxic physiology and strict caste systems, Grung are communal and hierarchical. They are highly territorial and survival-focused. This page contains the complete player-facing rules needed to select this option without opening any builder files.
statBlock.speed: Walking speed 30 ft.; swim speed or aquatic adaptation follows the selected lineage traits; swim speed 30 ft.; once on your turn, you can make the special leap, dash, or stride granted by the listed movement trait.
statBlock.abilityScores: +2 Dexterity; +1 Constitution. If the fixed line is not desired for this table, use the Belavadös flexible fallback: increase one ability by 2 and a different ability by 1, or increase three different abilities by 1. Recommended priorities: Wisdom, Constitution, Charisma.
statBlock.languages: Common plus Aquan or a local oceanic language.
statBlock.proficiencies: Skill proficiencies: Stealth, Perception, Survival. Additional proficiencies: water vehicles or navigator tools when appropriate.
